title: Only 20 days left in the $100k AI game jam, and I'm surprised almost nobody here is posting entries yet
author: Scart4000
selftext:
Just found this sub and honestly it feels like I finally landed in the right place with people actually building real games with AI.

I searched the sub before posting and was surprised how quiet it's been about the OpenGame.io $100k jam.

In case you missed it, it runs until Dec 18 and it's free to enter as a solo dev. Anything with a web export works (Three.js, Godot, Unity, Unreal, custom engines, whatever you use) and AI tools / vibe coding are completely allowed.

**Just to be clear, I'm not affiliated with them at all**. I'm competing myself, and I just love good competition.

Plus, let's be honest: people outside communities like this love to clown on AI game devs and vibe coders, saying we can only ship throwaway prototypes that aren't actually fun to play. A public $100k jam feels like a pretty good stage to prove them wrong and show real games with actual polish can come out of here.

The video above is the teaser I just cut for my entry, Nodo. I'm building the whole thing solo with AI coding agents and a lot of back and forth to nail the atmosphere and feel.

Shameless self-plug to wrap up: I'm posting daily build in public clips on my [X profile](https://x.com/itsolodavid?s=11&t=l7Elh8rRNjjfCZmCDNrE2g) if you want to follow along or trade notes.

Anyone else here jumping in?
